title: Disorder at the Cosmological Collider: Quenched Random Fields
summary: Cosmological-collider signals are usually interpreted as clean probes of massive particles present during inflation. In this work, we study a massive spectator field excited by a spatially quenched random source, which may arise from a frozen realization of a light field or environmental sector whose relaxation time is long compared with the inflationary timescale. We determine which features of the collider signal remain reliable probes of the heavy field.
